title: Universal localizations glue across monomorphic simplicial pushouts
statement: Use simplicial sets, degreewise products and pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and universal localization of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. A monomorphism means a degreewise injection; pushouts are formed degreewise. Let $A_{01}\to A_0$, $A_{01}\to A_1$ and $B_{01}\to B_0$, $B_{01}\to B_1$ be spans of small simplicial sets, with a strictly commuting map of spans $(f_{01},f_0,f_1)$. Assume that $A_{01}\to A_0$ and $B_{01}\to B_0$ are monomorphisms and that $f_{01},f_0,f_1$ are universally localizing. Then the induced map $A_0\amalg_{A_{01}}A_1\to B_0\amalg_{B_{01}}B_1$ is universally localizing. No injectivity is required of the other legs or vertical maps, and none of these simplicial sets is required to be a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA): both pushout squares, monomorphism legs and three universally localizing vertical maps; Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Write $A=A_0\amalg_{A_{01}}A_1$, $B=B_0\amalg_{B_{01}}B_1$, and $f:A\to B$ for the induced map. Fix any small map $g:T\to B$. For $i=0,1,01$ put $\bar B_i=T\times_B B_i$, $\bar A_i=T\times_B A_i$, where $A_i\to B$ is the composite through $f_i$. Then $\bar A_i\cong\bar B_i\times_{B_i}A_i$, with both maps given by the same pair of coordinates. The induced $\bar f_i:\bar A_i\to\bar B_i$ is universally localizing: a further pullback along $R\to\bar B_i$ is exactly $R\times_{B_i}A_i\to R$, covered by the definition for $f_i$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA), proof; base-change reduction, canonical edge collections and categorical pushout gluing. The categorical gluing argument is expanded using the existing isofibration and functor-calculus nodes.

proof.text: Both pulled-back spans have the original monomorphic leg: equality of pairs reduces injectivity to the corresponding map $A_{01}\to A_0$ or $B_{01}\to B_0$. Their degreewise pushouts are respectively $\bar A=T\times_B A$ and $\bar B=T$. Explicitly, a degree-$n$ pair $(t,[a])$ with equal images in $B_n$ is sent to the class of $(t,a)$ for a representative $a$ in either summand. Every generating pushout relation comes from an element of $A_{01,n}$; it preserves the image in $B_n$ and hence lifts to the relation for that element paired with $t$. This defines the inverse of the pushout comparison and commutes with all simplicial operators. The identical argument applies to the $B_i$. Thus it suffices to prove localization for this new map of monomorphic pushout spans.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA), proof; base-change reduction, canonical edge collections and categorical pushout gluing. The categorical gluing argument is expanded using the existing isofibration and functor-calculus nodes.

proof.text: For each $i$ let $W_i$ consist of edges of $\bar A_i$ having degenerate image under $\bar f_i$ in $\bar B_i$. By [lem-coef-universal-localization-degenerate-edges], for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, restriction is a functor equivalence $L_i:\operatorname{Fun}(\bar B_i,\mathcal E)\to M_i$, where $M_i\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\bar A_i,\mathcal E)$ is the full edge-inverting subcategory. If $u_i:\bar A_{01}\to\bar A_i$ is a span leg and $w\in W_{01}$, then $\bar f_i(u_iw)$ is the image of a degenerate edge under the corresponding simplicial map $\bar B_{01}\to\bar B_i$, so it is degenerate. Hence $u_i(W_{01})\subseteq W_i$. Restriction therefore gives a cospan $M_0\to M_{01}\leftarrow M_1$. All its objects are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA), proof; base-change reduction, canonical edge collections and categorical pushout gluing. The categorical gluing argument is expanded using the existing isofibration and functor-calculus nodes.

proof.text: Fix $\mathcal E$. The degreewise functor definition identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\bar B,\mathcal E)$ with the strict pullback of $\operatorname{Fun}(\bar B_0,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\bar B_{01},\mathcal E)\leftarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\bar B_1,\mathcal E)$: maps out of the pushout times $\Delta^n$ are compatible pairs of maps on its summands. Products with $\Delta^n$ preserve this pushout by the same representative calculation as step 2. Since $\bar B_{01}\to\bar B_0$ is degreewise injective, [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] says the left restriction is an isofibration. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]: this strict pullback, with these restriction maps, is the coherent pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The same degreewise identification and isofibration assertion hold for the full functor categories on the $\bar A_i$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA), proof; base-change reduction, canonical edge collections and categorical pushout gluing. The categorical gluing argument is expanded using the existing isofibration and functor-calculus nodes.

proof.text: The restricted left map $M_0\to M_{01}$ is still an isofibration. For an inner horn with vertices in $M_0$, use the ambient isofibration to fill it; every vertex of the filler is already a horn vertex, so fullness puts the filler in $M_0$. For an equivalence from the restriction of $F\in M_0$ to $G\in M_{01}$, lift in the ambient functor categories to an equivalence $F\to F^{\prime}$. Its components are equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For $w:x\to y$ in $W_0$, the naturality square in $h\mathcal E$ reads $[F^{\prime}(w)][\eta_x]=[\eta_y][F(w)]$. Composition and the equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] show $F^{\prime}(w)$ is an equivalence, since the other three edges have invertible classes. Thus $F^{\prime}\in M_0$; fullness retains the lifted equivalence and its inverse witnesses. This proves both lifting conditions without requiring either $\bar A_i$ to be a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA), proof; base-change reduction, canonical edge collections and categorical pushout gluing. The categorical gluing argument is expanded using the existing isofibration and functor-calculus nodes.

proof.text: Let $j_i:\bar A_i\to\bar A$ be the pushout inclusions and put $W=j_0(W_0)\cup j_1(W_1)$, a collection of degree-one simplices of $\bar A$. Let $M$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\bar A,\mathcal E)$ inverting $W$. Under step 4's strict pullback identification for $\bar A$, an object belongs to $M$ exactly when both of its summand restrictions belong to $M_0,M_1$. Those restrictions then belong to $M_{01}$ on the overlap by step 3. The same equality holds on all simplices, because all these subcategories are full, defined by their vertices. Consequently $M=M_0\times_{M_{01}}M_1$ as simplicial sets, compatibly with both projections. Step 5 and [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] show this is also the coherent pullback of the edge-inverting cospan.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.14 (02MA), proof; base-change reduction, canonical edge collections and categorical pushout gluing. The categorical gluing argument is expanded using the existing isofibration and functor-calculus nodes.

proof.text: Put $X_i=\operatorname{Fun}(\bar B_i,\mathcal E)$ with the strict pullback $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E)=X_0\times_{X_{01}}X_1$ of step 4, and $M=M_0\times_{M_{01}}M_1$ of step 6. For $G:\bar B_i\to\mathcal E$ and $v_i:\bar B_{01}\to\bar B_i$, $(G\bar f_i)u_i=(Gv_i)\bar f_{01}$, so the $L_i$ of step 3 commute strictly with overlap restriction and induce $\varphi=(L_0,L_1)$ between the strict pullbacks with $\operatorname{pr}_i\varphi=L_i\operatorname{pr}_i$. On $G:T\to\mathcal E$ its $j_i$-restrictions are those of $G\bar f$, so $\varphi=\bar f^*$. By steps 4–6 and [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] both projection squares are pullback squares in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The $L_i$ are equivalences in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, and by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] for the cospan shape they form an equivalence of cospan diagrams. Composed with it, the square of $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E)$ is a square over $M_0\to M_{01}\leftarrow M_1$, still limiting by the invariance under equivalences of cospan diagrams in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion]. Then $\varphi$ is a map of cones between two limiting squares on that cospan; by the naturality of the comparisons in maps of cones in the same node, for every small quasicategory $Q$ postcomposition $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E))^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,M)^\simeq$ is homotopic to one comparison equivalence followed by an inverse of the other. With $Q=M$ choose $\psi$ with $\varphi\psi$ naturally equivalent to the identity; with $Q=\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E)$, $\varphi\psi\varphi\simeq\varphi$ gives $\psi\varphi\simeq\mathrm{id}$. So $\bar f^*:\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E)\to M$ is a functor equivalence. As $W$ does not depend on $\mathcal E$, by [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map], $\bar f$ exhibits $T$ as the localization of $T\times_BA$ at $W$; since $g$ was arbitrary, $f$ is universally localizing.
